chapter: Complaints to Senator Eastland, FCC and WDSU
title: Letter to the Federal Radio and Television Commission
summary: La Rocca's complaint says WDSU broadcast untrue claims about the ODJB and refused him a script.

blocks.x: This is a follow-up letter that I wrote to Federal Radio Commission. Read my letter first underneath. This is a letter

headed D. James, Nicaragua, twenty-two eighteen Constance Street, New Orleans, Louisiana, thirteen. Federal Radio and Television Commission, Washington, D.C. Gentlemen, About eight months past, Station WDSU Television sold to one of their advertisers what was supposed to be the history of jazz music. I being the leader and manager of the world's first jazz band, Viz, the original Dixieland jazz band, they mentioned the original Dixieland jazz band and made many untrue statements, lies, also mentioned the personal of the band with a remark one of the members kept the books for the other boys. I being head of this band, this remark was uncalled for only to humiliate humiliate me among my friends. I'm sorry, I can't pronounce it. That's unbated. You're doing all right. I wrote this station for a script. They never answered my letter, so this is why I'm sending you this complaint. I've always thought that the airwaves were to be for the public service for all the people of this country and any station ceases to be for the public service when it becomes a mere profit of the people

can do the right for certain persons or factions or organizations interested in doing the thinking and judging and acting for the people. If this type of broadcasting is to continue, God help our country. I do not think any station has a right to mention a person's name over their network without that person's permission. The enclosed articles are all for the staff from my scrapbook. Chicago, Illinois, 1916. December 16, Ryzenweather's Cafe in New York City. London, England, 1919, 1920. Returned to New York City, 1920. Retired to New Orleans, 1926. Long before these radio or television was on the air. What action can I take against these people? Hoping you can give me some action on this matter. Sincerely yours, Leader and Manager, Regional Dixie Land Jazz Band, now retired.
